Each closed finding carries category (ConfigWiring, GuiBackendMapping, BackendGuiMapping, OperationSequence, KnownGaps), severity (Critical, Major, Minor, Info), nonempty message and nullable string suggestion. No failure-only `invalid_names` or `error_code` is synthesized for a passing/warning result. The completed result has no Critical or Major finding; zero findings and Minor/Info findings both pass. Save every settled result under its exact outcome, including a warning that policy permits to continue; this event never substitutes for the failed-family contract.

**Producer and transitions.** `Orchestrator backend / verify_tier_start / AfterTierStart` is the sole producer. It validates the StartVerificationResult against the original check and policy snapshot, settles that canonical result, and redacts it before preparing this event. State order is `checking → result_settled → append_pending → receipt_resolved → history_published`. Before append, the writer resolves this family's admission, exact schema, E9-2 retention assignment, original permission and Stop/scope fences. Missing or contradictory retention binding blocks current append. Commit any SP-337 pack first, then Case L append; adopt SP-286/CV-339 `storage.first_append_receipt.resolve.v2` full-value custody. Publish only after the durable first receipt. An uncertain result resolves the exact original value before retry, publication or dispatch decisions. History cannot rerun validation, spawn a provider/child, switch a model, change a budget, charge usage, send a warning notification or authorize continuation. Existing BeforeTierStart policy owns dispatch and blocking; warning is an overlay, not an Executor node status. A crash after result settlement repairs only the missing history append. Restore never recycles operation entropy or converts an uncertain append into a new observation.

evidence.quote: **Custody and redaction.** Storage owns seglog/packs, exact first receipt and original complete value; the verification operation owns its immutable settled result. Storage instance, opaque commit-group digest and original segment reference join Storage’s independently issued record. A retained read selects one recipe only from an independently sealed exact-original receipt and store snapshot through `RetainedDispatcher`; no read creates a receipt, guesses by family/Store recognition or tries a weaker fallback. This newly introduced family has only `ea-do-rfc8785-v2`; the failed family's older `ea-do-json-v1` edition is not evidence that old sibling records exist. Freeze schemas/recipe resources at original issuance and verify the complete original binding, source, producer digest and physical full-value commitment. Current writer policy, live findings and dispatch status cannot rewrite retained facts. Sanitize finding messages/suggestions before append; do not log credentials, raw configuration secrets or provider tokens. Current disclosure access, tombstone and hold restrictions still apply. A hold preserves custody and does not grant read access. Coherent backup/restore preserves original source, receipt, packs and recipe; a projection alone cannot reconstruct them.

History cannot rerun validation, spawn a provider/child, switch a model, change a budget, charge usage, send a warning notification or authorize continuation. Existing BeforeTierStart policy owns dispatch and blocking; warning is an overlay, not an Executor node status. A crash after result settlement repairs only the missing history append. Restore never recycles operation entropy or converts an uncertain append into a new observation.

**Consumers and checkpoints.** `reader.orchestrator.config_validation_passed.history.v1@1.0.0` serves the existing Orchestrator verification history/diagnostic inspector. It adopts SP-278's `reader.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0` and sole `projector.storage.event_record_index@1.0.0`, closed `Plans/event_record_index_checkpoint.schema.json#/$defs/checkpoint`, `event_record_index_checkpoint.v1:{storage_instance_id}` and `event_record_index.v2@{generation_id}`; family cursor is `none_required`. The generic owner validates the complete all-scope retained dataset/CURRENT/manifest, source/frame locators, generation birth/frontier, gaps and synced watermarks before family filtering. Acquire all ten read_token fields in one actual redb snapshot; CAS publication is the generic owner's transaction. Same-generation nonmatching appends and changed access/deletion/hold fences invalidate the old token and discard disclosure. **Compatibility and withdrawal.** New append/retry accepts only this exact schema/version and dedupe policy. Each of the four EventRecord migration members is null for these first-version families; no predecessor history is admitted. `projector_replay_only` is a historical reader mode and refuses current append. Retained originals require original admission/schema proof plus an explicitly supported active or compatibility reader. Writer withdrawal, first-receipt settlement and reader publication fencing are ordered; reader withdrawal or a changed publication epoch refuses disclosure without withdrawing the shared generic index. A successor requires its own closed schema, frozen recipe and governed generic rebuild before publication. The three outcomes stay distinct; no alias or status coercion turns failed/old text into this family.
